clean_source_blocks.text: Surveillance video released by Donald Trump shows the suspect running past metal detectors as security agents draw their guns.

What to know about the shooting at the White House Correspondents' DinnerInvestigators believe that the gunman who charged a security checkpoint outside the White House Correspondents' Dinner Saturday was targeting Trump administration officials, Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan."The suspect is in custody and has been identified as 31-year-old Cole Allen of Torrance California, multiple sources told CBS News. He was armed with a shotgun, a handgun and knives, and is believed to have acted alone, police said. Authorities said they have "preliminary information" that Allen was a guest at the Washington Hilton Hotel, where the event was being held. As part of the probe into his motives, investigators are reviewing writing by Allen that was found in the hotel.A Secret Service agent was struck by a round but was wearing a bulletproof vest and is expected to be OK, law enforcement sources said. President Trump and members of his administration were safely evacuated following the shooting. The president returned to the White House and held a news conference, praising officers for their response and telling Americans, "We have to resolve our differences." He said the dinner would be rescheduled and held within the next 30 days. Raskin says Trump's comments after shooting are "welcome change in rhetoric"
US police say the suspected gunman at the White House correspondents' dinner had multiple weapons on him when he charged a security checkpoint.

In an uncaptioned post on Truth Social, a shirtless man - believed to be the gunman at a shooting incident at the White House Correspondents' dinner on Apr 25, 2026, is seen lying prone on the ground. (Photo: Truth Social/Donald Trump)
